newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges Hun Sen to reconsider ASEAN push.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Hun Sen to reconsider ASEAN push.

text.p: The United States on Monday urged Cambodia strongman Hun Sen to reconsider his decision not to cooperate with a regional mediation effort for his crisis-ridden country.

"The United States very much regrets Mr. Hun Sen's rejection of the ASEAN efforts at mediation, because we consider the ASEAN initiative a very constructive one," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
"And we hope very much that he and his colleagues in Phnom Penh will reconsider the constructive proposal put to him" by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, he said.
Hun Sen, who had been Cambodia's second prime minister, took sole power July 6 when he ousted Prince Norodom Ranariddh, the first prime minister, in a military takeover.
He rejected ASEAN efforts to broker a solution to the crisis after the grouping delayed Cambodia's entry following the July 5-6 fighting and coup.
In recent days, Hun Sen has complained about outside interference in his country.
But Burns said the United States and other countries have every right to be involved and to comment on events there.

Washington and other capitals "helped resurrect Cambodia (after years of war and instability) through the 1991 Paris peace accords ... and it's been our international aid -- all of us together -- that has essentially allowed Mr. Hun Sen and Prince Ranariddh to have a start in coalition government in 1993, to get their feet in the ground," he said.
A U.S. special envoy, former congressman Stephen Solarz, is in Asia consulting various governments in an effort to formulate a coherent initiative on Cambodia.
He will report to Secretary of State Madeleine Albright when they rendezvous on Saturday at the ASEAN annual meeting in Kuala Lumpur, where Cambodia is expected to be a major issue.
